notes:
User wants automatic backups for important working files. They initially chose Google Drive because they already use it and purchased the 100 GB Google storage plan, then completed its setup. Important correction: Google Drive for desktop mainly synchronizes selected folders/files; it is not a full-system backup and normally does not provide scheduled backup failure alerts or whole-computer snapshots. Google Drive versioning is automatic and does not require a separate setting. Verify important files appear both locally and on the web, enable account security/2FA and relevant notifications, monitor shared Gmail/Google Photos/Drive storage, and ideally follow 3-2-1 with periodic restore tests.

User is now leaning toward/has chosen Backblaze as a genuine backup option. They asked about file versioning; prior advice claiming Backblaze keeps versions for up to 30 days and supports restoring to specific points should be verified against their current plan and Backblaze’s present policy before repeating it. If recommending it, distinguish backup from synchronization and check supported OS, encryption, external-drive handling, and version history/restore behavior.

User plans to clean laptop fans and now confirms they have a spare screwdriver, so no need to advise buying one unless the model requires a different tool. Future internal-laptop advice should still identify the exact model, power down/unplug, and address battery/internal-component safety.

User wants to organize their computer bag and chose an Anker cable organizer because it likely fits. They are troubleshooting a wireless mouse that freezes and plan to reset it using the manufacturer’s instructions first; if that fails, update drivers from the manufacturer, restart, and reconnect the receiver or Bluetooth device. Basic checks include battery/charge, receiver placement, wireless interference, and testing another USB port/receiver or mouse. Ask for mouse make/model, connection type, and symptoms before giving model-specific instructions.
